answers.answer: B) Run the container interactively with docker run -it <image> /bin/sh to inspect the environment and run the entrypoint manually. This is the most direct debugging approach because it lets you: (1) see the actual error output from the entrypoint script, (2) check environment variables, (3) verify file permissions and paths, (4) manually execute the entrypoint to see where it fails. Options A, C, and D don't address the root cause - the container is exiting due to an error in the entrypoint or application, not cache/memory/daemon issues.

## 1. GitHub Actions Workflow (.github/workflows/migrate.yml)

```yaml
name: Database Migration
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Tests"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  migrate:
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      
      - name: Create RDS Snapshot
        id: snapshot
        uses: aws-actions/aws-cli@v2
        with:
          aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
          aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
          aws-region: us-east-1
          command: rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier mydb --db-snapshot-identifier pre-migrate-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
      
      - name: Wait for Snapshot
        run: aws rds wait db-snapshot-completed --db-snapshot-identifier ${{ steps.snapshot.outputs.snapshot-id }}
      
      - name: Install Prisma
        run: npm install -g prisma
      
      - name: Run Migration
        id: migrate
        run: prisma migrate deploy
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}
      
      - name: Verify Migration
        run: |
          psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT version FROM _prisma_migrations ORDER BY finished_at DESC LIMIT 1;"
          psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users;"  # sanity check
      
      - name: Notify on Failure
        if: failure()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1
        with:
          payload: {"text": "Migration failed! Manual intervention required."}
```

## 2. Pre-migration Check Script (scripts/pre-migrate-check.sh)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY duration DESC LIMIT 10;"
psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"
psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT schemaname, tablename, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(schemaname||'.'||tablename)) FROM pg_tables ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size DESC;"
# Check migration is backward-compatible: review migration file for breaking changes
```

## 3. Rollback Procedure

```bash
# Restore from snapshot:
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier mydb-restored --db-snapshot-identifier pre-migrate-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS

# Or run migration down:
prisma migrate down --name "rollback_migration"

# Verify data integrity:
psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM critical_table;"
```

## 4. Migration Safety Checklist

- [ ] Migration is backward-compatible (old code works with new schema)
- [ ] No long-running queries will block the migration
- [ ] Backup snapshot created and verified
- [ ] Migration tested in staging environment
- [ ] Rollback procedure documented and tested
- [ ] Team notified of migration window
- [ ] Monitoring alerts configured during migration
- [ ] Migration file reviewed by another engineer
